correctness.rationale: Independent finite checks rebuilt the graph, both from the pentagonal rims and from the cyclic permutations of (0, ±1, ±φ) with edge length 2. Testing all 4,096 subsets by the edge/component forest identity reproduced the forest vector (1,12,66,200,345,300,60), no larger forest, and induced-edge minima 5 and 8 at sizes 6 and 7. The local five-cycle excludes an induced forest vertex of degree three, so every size-six forest is a connected P₆. All sixty have forest complements. For all named masks, exchange means popcount(A XOR B)=2, and every such replacement uses an original edge. Exact BFS gives a connected four-regular graph with 120 edges, 30+30 bipartition, girth 6 by deletion of each edge and shortest alternative paths, and common shells (1,4,12,17,16,9,1). The joint (Johnson distance, exchange distance, unordered count) entries reproduced are (1,1,120), (2,2,360), (2,3,150), (3,3,360), (3,4,120), (4,4,360), (4,5,150), (5,5,120), (6,6,30). All thirty distance-six pairs are complements; exactly 420 pairs take one extra move. This exhausts the fixed graph, not arbitrary polyhedra. Frozen replay paths: verify_partition.py, verify_partition.cpp, verify_python.out and verify_cpp.out in the record directory; uploaded code was inspected, not executed in the independent check.

value.rationale: Equitable induced-forest bisections of a canonical Platonic graph give a specific constrained reconfiguration problem. The complete intrinsic-versus-ambient distance classification tells which pairs cannot use a shortest Johnson path and how many require one extra move; the local-edge rule and unique complement antipodes also distinguish the exchange geometry. These facts are useful beyond the known face census, for example as exact small benchmarks for constrained path-partition reconfiguration. No generalization beyond this graph is needed for that use.
